govdocs-archive_org-nsia-DomesticIntelli: This item — Domestic Intelligence King — is a National Security Internet Archive file on the FBI’s King surveillance. The file’s full context is unclear. The Bureau spied on King for years. The item is a fragment of the civil-rights archive.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-InvestigationKi: This FBI report — Investigation of the Assassination of Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. — is a Bureau file. The declassified report is a primary source. The King manhunt was massive. Researchers value such files. The file belongs to the government archive.
myths-and-legends-of-our-own-land-volume: Charles Skinner opens his great folklore collection along the Hudson River and its hills. Ghosts of Dutch settlers, Revolutionary soldiers, and river pirates haunt these tales gathered from local legend. The volume shows Skinner's gift for making America's backyard as rich in story as any old country.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-adalbert-i: This 1913 reference article on Adalbert I — the medieval German prelate of stormy times. John Joseph A'Becket gives his career. Church and empire tugged at his loyalty. A prince-bishop of the old Reich. His name survives in charters and chronicles. The empire's bishops were princes then.
